title: How KryBit Ransomware Works and How to Test Your Defenses
content_md: Key Takeaways KryBit is a Ransomware-as-a-Service operation launched in late March 2026, leasing encryption builders to affiliates. Builders cover Windows, Linux, VMware ESXi, and NAS devices, extending encryption across endpoints, servers, virtualization, and network storage. Double extortion stages 10 GB to 250 GB per victim before encryption, with ransoms of $40,000 to $100,000. Rival group 0APT breached the administrator panel on 13 April 2026, exposing two administrators, five affiliates, and twenty negotiations. Operations continued after the leak, surpassing 50 claimed victims by the close of the first full quarter. The Picus Platform simulates KryBit ransomware attacks so teams can validate security controls against this threat. KryBit is a Ransomware-as-a-Service operation that launched in late March 2026 with builders for Windows, Linux, VMware ESXi, and NAS devices, staging 10 GB to 250 GB of victim data before encrypting files with a fixed .KRYBIT extension and dropping a RECOVER-README.txt ransom note [1].
